Best Portable Power Stations Under $1,000 (2026)

WattList may earn a commission if you buy through links on this page, at no extra cost to you. Rankings are not for sale. Samples are disclosed when a brand provided the unit.

Direct answer (2026, under $1,000): For most buyers, pick the Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2 (1,024 Wh, 2,000 W continuous, ~24.9 lb, wall full in about 49 minutes on UltraFast). Want the most watt-hours per dollar in this band? Bluetti AC180 (1,152 Wh, often ~$450Ã¢â‚¬â€œ$500 street). Need the lightest ~1 kWh daily driver? Jackery Explorer 1000 v2 (1,070 Wh, 23.8 lb). Planning to add capacity later? EcoFlow DELTA 3 (1,024 Wh, expandable toward ~5 kWh). Small apartment loads without a full-size fridge? EcoFlow RIVER 2 Pro (768 Wh).

WattList sizes kits with usable AC watt-hours in mind: nameplate Wh is not what you get at the wall after inverter loss. Street prices move weekly Ã¢â‚¬â€ confirm on the retailer page before you buy.

Specs checked against manufacturer pages; street prices sampled Sep 2026. Affiliate links may earn WattList a commission; rankings are not for sale.

If you want a portable power station under $1,000 in 2026, you are shopping in the sweet spot: enough watt-hours for a weekend fridge, a short blackout, or a van night â€” without hauling a 50 lb brick or paying whole-home backup money.

This guide is for people who will actually carry the unit, plug real loads into it, and care about Wh, output watts, LiFePO4 cycle life, ports, weight, and recharge speed more than marketing slogans.

How we picked (buying criteria that matter)

Ignore â€œsolar generatorâ€ branding. These are lithium battery + inverter boxes. Judge them on:

1. Capacity (Wh)

Watt-hours = how much energy is in the tank. Rough mental model for a ~1,000 Wh unit (after ~85â€“90% usable inverter efficiency):

Router + phone charging: many hours / overnight easy
12V compressor fridge (intermittent ~30â€“60 W average): often a full day+
Mini fridge + lights + devices: plan carefully; may need solar or a mid-day top-up

If you need fridge + Wiâ€‘Fi + overnight CPAP-class loads, read our sizing notes below â€” and check your deviceâ€™s label wattage; for CPAP, talk to the manufacturer about DC options and humidifier draw. We do not make medical claims.

2. Output (continuous W + surge)

Continuous watts must clear your hungriest device. A 1,500 W inverter covers most camp kettles and induction-adjacent fantasies less well than people hope â€” check the kettle. Fridges and tools care about surge. So do sump pumps: our sump pump guide checks six stations against 1/3 to 3/4 horsepower starting watts. Prefer units that publish both continuous and surge ratings.

3. Chemistry: LiFePO4 vs NMC

In 2026, almost everything worth buying under $1k is LiFePO4 â€” typically marketed around 3,000â€“4,000+ cycles to a residual capacity threshold. Older NMC packs are lighter for the same Wh but age faster. Prefer LiFePO4 unless you have a specific weight constraint and accept shorter calendar life.

4. Ports

Count what you will use the same hour:

AC outlets (2â€“6)
USB-C Power Delivery (look for 100 W if you charge a laptop from USB-C)
USB-A, 12V car outlet, sometimes wireless pad
Solar XT60 / Anderson / brand proprietary input
5. Weight and form factor

A 1 kWh LiFePO4 pack usually lands ~23â€“36 lb (Jackery 1000 v2 23.8 lb, Anker C1000 Gen 2 24.9 lb, DELTA 3 27.6 lb, AC180 35.3 lb). That difference matters when you are loading a hatchback or storing under a van bench. Jackeryâ€™s 1000 v2 is the â€œI will actually carry thisâ€ benchmark; Bluetti AC180 trades weight for Wh and output.

6. Recharge (wall + solar + car)

Wall recharge under ~1â€“2 hours is table stakes for mid-range 2026 units. Solar input caps (200â€“600 W+ on this class) decide whether you can recover overnight camping use with one foldable panel. Car charging is slow â€” treat it as top-up, not primary.

Best overall under $1,000: Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2

Who itâ€™s for: Campers and apartment dwellers who want a 1,024 Wh LiFePO4 pack that recharges fast from the wall and can shove serious AC watts when a kettle or tool spikes.

Why it wins for many people: Official specs: 1,024 Wh, 2,000 W continuous / 3,000 W peak, 24.9 lb, 600 W solar, 4,000 cycles to 80%. UltraFast wall charge is 0â€“100% in 49 minutes at 1,600 W (enable in the Anker app; standard AC input is 1,200 W). App control and 10 ms uninterruptible power supply matter for desk setups and short outages. Gen 2 is not expandable (the original C1000 is) â€” that is the trade for the smaller, lighter box.

Pros

Fastest published wall recharge in this class (49 min UltraFast)
Highest continuous output here (2,000 W) at 24.9 lb
LiFePO4, 4,000 cycles to 80%
10 ports including dual 140 W USB-C; 10 ms uninterruptible power supply

Cons

Fans can get noticeable under load (common complaint in this class)
No expansion battery â€” buy the original C1000 if you need that path
Brand ecosystem for solar panels is competitive, not uniquely cheap
List is $799; the pick assumes you buy on a typical $430â€“$530 street sale

Shop: Check Amazon price â€” check Amazon and Anker direct; use whichever is cheaper after shipping. Amazon primary (no Anker brand affiliate mid yet)

Best capacity per dollar: Bluetti AC180

Who itâ€™s for: Buyers who want maximum Wh and AC headroom under the $1k cap and do not mind 35.3 lb.

Why it lands here: Official specs: 1,152 Wh, 1,800 W continuous / 2,700 W Power Lifting Mode, 35.3 lb, 500 W solar, 3,500+ cycles to 80%. Turbo AC input is 1,440 W â€” 0â€“80% in 45 minutes, 0â€“100% in 1.3â€“1.8 hours. Dense ports include a 15 W wireless pad and a 100 W USB-C. Street price is often the lowest in this 1 kWh set (~$450â€“$500; $499 on brand site and Amazon as of 5 Sep 2026). If your use case is car camping with a fridge and you load from a hatch â€” not a long hike â€” weight is fine. No native extra-battery expansion (Bluetti FAQ: B80/B230/B300 can only charge the AC180 in Power Bank mode).

Pros

Highest capacity among common sub-$1k 1 kWh rivals
Strong inverter (1,800 W) plus 2,700 W lifting mode for resistive heat loads
LiFePO4 longevity (3,500+ to 80%); 5-year warranty; mature Bluetti app

Cons

Heaviest here vs Jackery 1000 v2 (23.8 lb) / Anker C1000 Gen 2 (24.9 lb)
Wall/solar recharge is good, not class-leading vs Anker 49 min / EcoFlow 56 min
Bulkier storage footprint in a small apartment closet
Not expandable the way EcoFlow Delta extras are

Shop: Check Amazon price | Buy at BLUETTI

Code watt5 â€” 5% off at BLUETTI (excl. accessories & flash sales). Soft check: Power Week if a deal beats street price.

Also consider: ALLPOWERS R1500 (expandable value)

Who itâ€™s for: Shoppers who want AC180-class watt-hours under $1,000 and may want to add extra batteries later â€” and will accept a less mainstream brand than Bluetti / Jackery / EcoFlow / Anker.

Why it sits here as an also-consider: Official US specs: 1,152 Wh, 1,800 W continuous / 3,000 W surge, LiFePO4 (3,500+ cycles), 36.8 lb, 650 W solar, 15-millisecond backup switch, expandable with up to 3Ã— B1000 (to 4,608 Wh). Brand street as of 21 Sep 2026: $539 sale / $899 list â€” often the cheapest path to this Wh/output combo when in stock. It does not replace the Anker / Jackery / Bluetti / EcoFlow primary picks; treat it as a value alt when stock and shipping look clean.

Pros

Same 1,152 Wh tank as Bluetti AC180 at a lower typical street price
Real expansion path (B1000 extras) unlike AC180 / Jackery 1000 v2 / Anker C1000 Gen 2
650 W solar ceiling and 1,800 W inverter for fridge + camp loads

Cons

Heavier than Jackery 1000 v2 (23.8 lb) / Anker C1000 Gen 2 (24.9 lb)
Smaller review base and support footprint than the big four
Brand pages flip between in stock and sold out â€” live-check before you buy

Shop: ALLPOWERS R1500

Optional panel match (200 W foldable, solar-connector / MC4-class with XT60 adapter in box): ALLPOWERS SP033 200 W

Best lightweight ~1 kWh: Jackery Explorer 1000 v2

Who itâ€™s for: Weekend camping, overlanding day-to-day carry, anyone who has abandoned a heavy â€œdealâ€ unit in the garage.

Why it wins on usability: Official specs: 1,070 Wh, 1,500 W rated / 3,000 W surge, LiFePO4, 4,000 cycles to 70%+, 23.8 lb, 400 W max solar (dual DC8020). Standard wall charge is 1.58 hours; Emergency Super Charge (Jackery app) is ~59 minutesâ€“1 hour 0â€“100%. It is not expandable. It is rarely the fastest charger or the most expandable box â€” it is the one you will actually put in the car every Friday.

Pros

Best weight-to-capacity feel in the ~1 kWh club (23.8 lb)
Simple interface; strong brand accessory ecosystem (SolarSaga)
Enough AC for fridge + devices for most weekend trips; â‰¤20 ms uninterruptible power supply

Lower continuous watts than Anker C1000 Gen 2 (2,000 W) / Bluetti AC180 (1,800 W)
No battery expansion (use Explorer 1000 Plus if you need that)
Solar input cap (400 W) is adequate, not maximal

Shop: Jackery Explorer 1000 v2

Best if you might expand: EcoFlow DELTA 3 / DELTA 3 Plus

Who itâ€™s for: Van life or blackout shoppers who suspect 1 kWh will not be enough in a year.

Why include it under $1k: Official DELTA 3 specs: 1,024 Wh, 1,800 W / 3,600 W surge, X-Boost 2,200 W, 27.6 lb, 500 W solar, 1,500 W AC in, 0â€“100% in 56 minutes, 4,000 cycles to 80%+, <10 ms uninterruptible power supply, expandable to 5 kWh (DELTA 3 / DELTA 2 / DELTA 2 Max / DELTA Pro 3 extra batteries). Brand street as of 5 Sep 2026: $629 sale / $699 regular â€” comfortably under $1k. Labor Day 2026 listings were ~$599.

DELTA 3 Plus is the same 1,024 Wh / 1,800 W / 27.6 lb box with the meaningful upgrades: dual 500 W maximum power point tracking (MPPT) (1,000 W solar, ~70 min solar full), 2Ã— 140 W USB-C (vs 100 W), 2Ã— 36 W USB-A (vs 18 W). Brand: $719 sale / $799 regular (Labor Day ~$669). Solo Plus still clears $1k; Plus + extra battery (~$1,119â€“$1,299) does not. Confirm the exact model before you click. EcoFlow US pages sometimes show pre-order / restock language â€” check live ship date.

Pros

True extra-battery path (up to 5 kWh)
Fastest EcoFlow-class wall charge here (56 min)
Strong app, 13 ports, IP65 battery pack

Cons

Easy to blow the $1k cap once you add an extra battery or panel bundle
Weight creeps as you expand
More knobs = more ways to overbuy
Base unit is under $1k today; treat that as live-check, not a permanent ceiling

Shop: EcoFlow DELTA 3 Â· EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus

Best compact lane: EcoFlow RIVER 2 Pro (and RIVER 3 class)

Who itâ€™s for: Apartment blackout kits focused on router, phones, laptop, LED lights, CPAP without heavy humidifier loads â€” not a full-size fridge for two days.

RIVER 2 Pro official: 768 Wh, 800 W continuous / 1,600 W X-Boost and surge, 18.2 lb, 220 W solar, 0â€“100% in 70 minutes (0â€“80% ~56 min), LiFePO4 3,000 cycles to 80%+. EcoFlow US $349 sale / $529 list as of 5 Sep 2026 (sometimes listed sold out / pre-order).

RIVER 3 is a different, much smaller class: 245 Wh, 300 W (X-Boost 600 W), 7.8 lb, 110 W solar, ~$239. RIVER 3 Plus is 286 Wh / 600 W (X-Boost 1,200 W), ~10.4 lb, 220 W solar. Neither replaces a 1 kWh fridge weekend.

At 768 Wh you are buying portability and price. Pair with a clear load list. If your fridge is non-negotiable for 24+ hours, step up to a ~1 kWh unit above.

Pros

Easy to store and carry (18.2 lb for the Pro; 7.8 lb for RIVER 3)
Fast recharge relative to size (70 min full on RIVER 2 Pro)
Often the smartest first buy for urban users

Cons

Not enough Wh for heavy multi-day fridge duty
Lower continuous AC than 1 kWh flagships

Shop: EcoFlow RIVER 2 Pro Â· EcoFlow RIVER 3

Honorable mention: Jackery Explorer 2000 v2 (sale only)

Official: 2,042 Wh, 2,200 W / 4,400 W surge, LiFePO4 4,000 cycles to 70%+, 39.5 lb, 400 W max solar, Emergency Super Charge ~1.7 hours 0â€“100% (spec table AC adapter 1.75 hr). Not expandable.

As of 5 Sep 2026 it is already under $1k: Jackery.com $899 sale / $999 regular; Amazon listings have been around $799. Historical list was $1,499. If it climbs back over $1,000, skip it for this roundup and stick to the 1 kWh class.

Jackery Explorer 2000 v2

What size do you actually need?

Use this crude planner (device watts Ã— hours = Wh, then add ~20% overhead):

LOAD	EXAMPLE DRAW	HOURS	WH NEEDED
Wiâ€‘Fi router	10â€“20 W	24	240â€“480
Phones / tablets	5â€“15 W avg	24	120â€“360
12V compressor fridge	40 W avg	24	~960
Mini fridge (AC)	50â€“100 W avg	12â€“24	600â€“2,400
CPAP (check label)	device-dependent	8	varies
Add ~20% overhead. CPAP: check label / manufacturer â€” no medical claims.

CPAP note: Draws vary widely with humidifier and heated hose. Check your device wattage and talk to the manufacturer about approved DC cables and power options. A power station is just an inverter/battery â€” size it from real watts, not blog folklore.

If fridge + network + overnight medical-adjacent loads are all required, a single sub-$1k unit may cover a short outage but not a long one without solar. That is normal â€” do not overbuy â€œjust in caseâ€ without doing the math.

Wall vs solar recharge: set expectations
Wall: Mid-range 2026 units often hit full in roughly 1â€“2 hours. Published 0â€“100% fast modes: Anker C1000 Gen 2 49 min, EcoFlow DELTA 3 / 3 Plus 56 min, Jackery 1000 v2 Emergency ~1 hr (standard 1.58 hr), Bluetti AC180 turbo 1.3â€“1.8 hr (0â€“80% in 45 min).
Solar: A 200 W foldable panel in real sun might deliver ~120â€“160 W average. Replacing ~1,000 Wh can take a long sunny day â€” or two mediocre ones. Buy panel wattage for your latitude and season, not the brochure peak.
Car 12V: Slow. Fine for topping phonesâ€™ worth of energy on a drive, not for filling 1 kWh before camp.

Jackery SolarSaga 200W Â· EcoFlow 220W Bifacial Â· Bluetti PV200</a Â· ALLPOWERS SP033 200 W>

Who should spend less than $500 instead

If your list is phones, camera batteries, a router, and a CPAP without a fridge, a RIVER / Anker C800 / Bluetti EB or AC50-class unit often wins. Put the savings into a panel or a better cable kit. We will cover the under-$500 lane in a dedicated guide; until then, do not let this roundup upsell you past your loads.

FAQ
Will a 1,000 Wh power station run a fridge?

Often for hours to about a day, depending on the fridge, room temperature, and how often the door opens. Use average watts Ãƒâ€” hours, then add ~20% overhead. A 12V compressor fridge averaging ~40 W needs roughly ~960 Wh for 24 hours before overhead Ã¢â‚¬â€ so a ~1 kWh station is a planning starting point, not a guarantee.

LiFePO4 or NMC under $1,000?

Default to LiFePO4 in this price band for cycle life. Choose NMC only if weight is the binding constraint and you accept fewer cycles.

Is a Ã¢â‚¬Å“solar generatorÃ¢â‚¬Â different from a power station?

Usually no Ã¢â‚¬â€ marketing. You buy a battery + inverter station; solar panels are optional inputs.

What size do I need for fridge + WiÃ¢â‚¬â€˜Fi + overnight CPAP-class loads?

Add each load (watts Ãƒâ€” hours), then ~20% overhead. CPAP draw varies a lot with humidifier and heated hose Ã¢â‚¬â€ use the device label and the manufacturerÃ¢â‚¬â„¢s guidance; WattList does not make medical claims. Full walkthrough: How many Wh for fridge + WiÃ¢â‚¬â€˜Fi + CPAP?

Anker vs Bluetti vs Jackery vs EcoFlow under $1k Ã¢â‚¬â€ short version?
Anker C1000 Gen 2: best overall mix of charge speed, output, and weight.
Bluetti AC180: most Wh per dollar; heavier.
Jackery 1000 v2: lightest carry in the ~1 kWh club.
EcoFlow DELTA 3: best if you expect to add an extra battery later.
Can I use these indoors during a blackout?

Unlike gas generators, lithium power stations produce no exhaust. Keep vents clear, follow the manual, and do not cover cooling fans. They are commonly used indoors for routers, lights, and fridges.

Do I need Amazon or brand sites?

For Jackery, EcoFlow, and Bluetti, brand networks (Awin and similar) often pay better when we have them; Amazon is convenient and strong for Anker. Use the linked retailer that is cheaper that day Ã¢â‚¬â€ Amazon links use tag thewattlist20-20.

Bottom line
Most people under $1k: Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2 or Jackery Explorer 1000 v2 if weight rules.
Max Wh / output for the money: Bluetti AC180.
Also consider (value + expandable): ALLPOWERS R1500 â€” verify stock; optional SP033 200 W panel.

Code watt5 â€” 5% off at BLUETTI (excl. accessories & flash sales). Soft check: Power Week if a deal beats street price.

Might expand later: EcoFlow DELTA 3 (confirm price).
Small loads / first apartment kit: EcoFlow RIVER 2 Pro.

 #ad Prices are read from Amazon’s API and refreshed daily; the date each one was read is shown beside the buy buttons below, and a price that stops refreshing disappears rather than going stale. Weights and capacities are manufacturer-published figures; sources are listed at the foot of this page.
 Our pick
 Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2
 2,000W continuous out of 1,024Wh and 24.9 lb, with a full recharge in 49 minutes — the widest appliance envelope in the class.
 1,024Wh · 2,000W continuous · 24.9 lb · 600W solar in

 Read the full review first → 
 Start here, because the term is broken. '1000W' is an inverter rating — the maximum the unit can deliver at any instant. '1000Wh' is a battery capacity — how long it can deliver anything. They are different specifications, they are not interchangeable, and a listing that says '1000W Portable Power Station' in its title is usually describing a unit with around 1,000 watt-hours of battery and an inverter somewhere between 1,000W and 2,000W. If you are shopping on this phrase, the number you almost certainly care about is the watt-hours. 
 The four units below are the 1kWh class as it actually sells in the US right now: 1,024Wh to 1,152Wh of LiFePO4 battery, 1,500W to 2,000W of continuous output, and 23.8 lb to 35.27 lb to carry. Every figure here is read from the manufacturer's own specification page, linked at the bottom. We do not run a test lab and will not pretend to — how we choose sets out exactly what that means. 
 The class, side by side
 The 1kWh class on published manufacturer figures. Watt-hours per pound is our arithmetic on those numbers. Unit Battery Continuous Surge Weight Wh/lb Solar in Wall recharge 
 Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2 1,024Wh 2,000W 3,000W 24.9 lb 41.1 600W 49 min 
 EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus 1,024Wh 1,800W 3,600W 27.6 lb 37.1 1,000W 56 min

 Jackery Explorer 1000 v2 1,070Wh 1,500W 3,000W 23.8 lb 45.0 400W 1.7 hr 
 Read down the Wh/lb column and the spread is 38% between the lightest and the heaviest for roughly the same battery. Read down the solar column and the spread is 2.5x. Those are the two specifications that actually separate these units; capacity barely moves. 
 What 1,000 watt-hours runs
 Appliance figures below are nameplate bands. Read the plate on your own equipment — the sticker on the back or the base — because the spread inside a product category is wider than the spread between these units. 
 Runtime from about 1,024Wh of usable battery, by load. Load Typical draw Runtime 
 Router and modem 10-20W 2-3 days 
 Phone charging 10-15W 40-60 full charges 
 LED camp lights 5-15W Several days 
 CPAP, humidifier off 30-60W 2-3 nights 
 Laptop 45-65W 13-18 hours 
 12V camping fridge 45W cycling at 40% About 2 days 
 Full-size refrigerator 150W cycling at 35% Under a day 
 Starlink Mini 20-40W continuous About a day 
 Pellet grill after ignition 40-60W 16-24 hours 
 Electric kettle 1,500W About 8 boils 
 Microwave 1,200W About 40 min of cooking 
 Space heater 1,500W About 35 min 
 The bottom three rows are why we keep saying the same thing: a kilowatt-hour is days of electronics and minutes of heat. What can a 1000W power station run has the full version of that list, and what size power station do I need is the five-minute exercise that usually moves people a whole size band before they spend anything. 
 How to pick between the four
 Will anything that heats go into it? A kettle, a microwave, an electric griddle, a circular saw. If yes, take the 2,000W Anker and accept the two outlets. 1,500W is a hard ceiling, not a suggestion. 
 Will you buy panels? If yes, the EcoFlow's 1,000W of solar input is worth more than any other difference on the table, because it halves the time to refill. If no, you are paying for an input you will never use. 
 Will you carry it? If the unit goes from the car to a tent pad, 23.8 lb versus 35.27 lb is the whole decision and the Jackery wins it outright. 
 Does it live in a vehicle? Then weight stops mattering and the BLUETTI's extra 128Wh and 3,500-cycle rating become the argument. 
 How many things plug in at once? Two AC outlets is genuinely limiting at a campsite or a tailgate. The EcoFlow's six and the BLUETTI's four are not a luxury. 
 Where the class runs out
 A kilowatt-hour is the sweet spot of the category and it is also a ceiling. Three jobs sit outside it entirely, and buying a 1kWh unit for any of them ends in a second purchase. 
 Anything that heats a room. What size power station to run a space heater does the arithmetic; the answer is about 35 minutes. 
 An air conditioner. Even a small window unit empties this class in a couple of hours at best. What size power station to run a window air conditioner sets out what it actually takes. 
 Multi-day home backup. A full-size fridge alone is most of a kilowatt-hour a day. If an outage is the reason you are shopping, read what size power station for a power outage first and expect to be looking at 2kWh and up. 
 On price
 This site shows the live Amazon price inside each buy button rather than printing a number in the copy, because a figure typed into a page is wrong within a week. Every ranking above is made on published specifications and fit, never on a price claim. 
 If this class turns out to be more than you need, best budget power stations under $500 and best lightweight power stations cover the tier below. If it is not enough, best expandable power stations ranks the units that take a second battery, which is the cheap insurance against sizing this wrong. 
 If this class turns out to be a size too small, the tier above now has its own page. Best 2000W power stations ranks the 2 kWh units on the same four criteria and finds the same pattern one step up: capacity barely moves between them, while weight spreads 33% and recharge time spreads 2.4x. It is also where the output-versus-weight trade-off gets sharp - 2,600W costs you 53 lb, and the unit that avoids that bill is the subject of our Anker SOLIX C2000 Gen 2 review . 
 The two output figures on those spec sheets are not the same specification, and the difference decides whether a motor-driven appliance starts at all: surge watts vs running watts covers what each measures and where to read the matching pair off your own nameplate. For the units with the widest starting margin in the registry, best power station for high-surge loads ranks on peak rating alone. 
 The two units at the top of this class are worth looking at head to head rather than one after the other. Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2 vs EcoFlow DELTA 3 works through the only four specifications that actually separate them - continuous watts, outlet count, weight and whether the unit can be expanded later - and says plainly which way each one should push you. 
 There is a newer value entry in this class worth knowing about before you commit. The UDPOWER S1200 review covers 1,191Wh - the largest battery anyone sells at this size - at 26.0 lb, which is 45.8 watt-hours per pound and the best in the class. The catch is the inverter: 1,200W continuous and an 1,800W maximum are both the lowest figures here, so it runs fridges, fans, laptops and CPAPs for longer than anything on this page and will not boil a kettle at all.

Most units sold on that phrase pair a kilowatt-hour battery with a 1,000-1,500W inverter; this one gives you a full 2,000W continuous with a 3,000W surge, so a kettle, a microwave, a griddle or a circular saw is inside the envelope rather than right at the edge of it. 
 Anker publishes a full recharge in 49 minutes at 1,600W input, a 10 ms UPS switchover, 80% capacity after 4,000 cycles, a 5-year warranty and dimensions of 15.12 x 8.19 x 9.61 in. The 49-minute figure is the one that changes how you use the thing: you can top it up over lunch rather than planning a charge overnight. 
 24.9 lb works out at 41.1Wh per pound, a little behind the Jackery below. The real limits are two AC outlets and no expansion — if you want six outlets and a second battery, Anker's own previous generation still sells, and C1000 vs C1000 Gen 2 is the page that settles which one you want.

That is twice the Anker and twice the BLUETTI, and on a sunny day it is the difference between a unit that refills itself by lunchtime and one that is still working on it at dusk.

 27.6 lb is 37.1Wh per pound, the joint-worst figure of the four, and it is 2.7 lb heavier than the Anker for the same battery. If you only ever charge from a wall socket, the plain EcoFlow DELTA 3 is the same box with half the solar input and no reason to pay for the Plus.

 Jackery publishes 4,000 cycles to 70% capacity, a 1.7-hour wall recharge, a one-hour emergency charge through the app, below 22 decibels in silent mode, a switchover under 20 ms and a 5-year warranty with registration. Below 22 dB is quieter than every other unit here publishes, which matters inside a tent. 
 400W of solar input is the lowest of the four and it does not expand.  Questions
 Frequently asked questions
 Is a 1000W power station the same as a 1000Wh power station? + No. 1000W is the inverter's maximum instantaneous output; 1000Wh is how much energy the battery holds. A listing titled '1000W power station' usually means roughly 1,000 watt-hours of battery with an inverter between 1,000W and 2,000W. Check both numbers on the specification sheet before you buy. 
 What can a 1000W power station run? + Everything on a camping or desk list, for days: a router, phones, lights, a laptop, a CPAP without its heated humidifier, a 12V fridge. It will also run a kettle or a microwave in short bursts. What it will not do is heat or cool a room — a 1,500W space heater empties a kilowatt-hour in about 35 minutes. 
 Which 1000W power station is the lightest? + Of the four here, the Jackery Explorer 1000 v2 at 23.8 lb for 1,070Wh, which is 45.0 watt-hours per pound and the best ratio anywhere in this site's registry. The heaviest is the BLUETTI AC180 at 35.27 lb, which buys you 128Wh more battery and a longer cycle rating. 
 Can a 1000W power station run a refrigerator? + A full-size household fridge, yes, for somewhere under a day depending on how often the compressor cycles — but check the surge rating, because a compressor draws several times its running wattage for the first fraction of a second. A 12V camping fridge runs about two days on the same battery. 
 How long does a 1000W power station take to charge? + From a wall socket, between 49 minutes and 1.8 hours across these four, which is a bigger spread than it looks on a camping trip. From solar it depends entirely on the input ceiling: EcoFlow accepts 1,000W, Anker 600W, BLUETTI 500W and Jackery 400W. 
 Is 1000Wh enough for camping? + For most trips, yes, and comfortably. A 12V fridge, lights, phones and a camera battery is roughly 300-500Wh a day, which is a two- to three-night weekend without a panel. It is not enough if you are running a heater, a kettle for a group, or an electric cooker.

 The $500-$1,000 range is where portable power stations get serious. You unlock 1,000Wh+ capacity, 1,500W+ output, and LFP batteries that last for years. These stations handle camping, home backup, remote work, and even running small appliances.
 What $1,000 Gets You in 2026
 The sub-$1,000 tier in 2026 is remarkably competitive. Three years ago, a 1,000Wh LFP station with fast charging cost $1,500+. Today, multiple options exist under $1,000 with fast charging, UPS capability, and strong output power. The main differentiator between models is the balance of capacity, features, and weight.
 1. EcoFlow Delta 3 Plus — Best Overall
 The Delta 3 Plus is the most capable station under $1,000. At 1,024Wh with 1,800W output, it runs everything from laptops to microwaves. The 56-minute full charge is the fastest in its class. UPS functionality with sub-10ms switchover makes it a dual-purpose camping and home backup unit. At 25.4 lbs, it is also the lightest 1,000Wh+ station.
